title: anthropics/sandbox-runtime: a file and network fence without a container
friendlyTitle: sandbox-runtime limits the files and network a process can touch
summary: sandbox-runtime is an Apache-2.0 tool that enforces filesystem and network limits on a process at the operating-system level, without requiring a container. Anthropic uses this class of fence around coding-agent commands. The repository was updated on 24 October. GitHub's daily TypeScript trending list had it at 592 stars today. The repository has 6,435 stars.
friendlySummary: sandbox-runtime is a free tool that limits which files and network hosts a process can use. It does this at the operating-system level, without requiring a container. Anthropic uses this kind of fence around coding-agent commands. The repository was updated on 24 October. GitHub's daily TypeScript trending list had it at 592 stars today. The repository has 6,435 stars. The license is Apache-2.0.
whyItMatters: If an agent can run commands on your machine, this is a way to say which directories and which hosts that process may touch, instead of hoping the prompt holds. You still have to write the allow and deny rules. A sandbox does not decide whether the task itself was a good idea.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If an agent can run commands on your machine, this is a way to say which folders and which sites that process may touch, instead of hoping the instructions hold. You still have to write the allow and deny rules. A sandbox does not decide whether the task itself was a good idea.
